app.Response.description: The Response struct is used for wrapping the API response with a code, message, and data.

code.description:
Code is the HTTP status code or a custom code used to indicate the result of the request
@example 200

data.description:
Data is the response data (can be any object or null)
@example {"id": 1, "name": "John Doe"}

msg.description:
Msg is the message that describes the result of the request
@example "Request successful"

info.description: Crawlora is a hosted web-data and SERP API: call documented REST endpoints and get normalized JSON instead of HTML to parse — across search/SERP, maps and local, e-commerce, app stores, social, media and finance. One API key; Crawlora runs the proxy rotation, headless browsers and parsing behind the scenes. Billed pay-on-success: charged only on a successful 2xx response, 1-10 credits per call, with a free tier of 2,000 credits per month and no card. A hosted MCP server (mcp.crawlora.net/mcp) exposes the same catalog as agent tools. Search endpoints accept `q` as a universal alias for whichever search-term parameter they document (`query`, `term`, `keyword`, or Amazon's `k`), so one parameter name works across the whole catalog; an explicitly supplied documented name always wins.

get.description:
Returns normalized YouTube search results using YouTube's InnerTube search API.
Pass `continuation_token` from a previous response to retrieve the next page.
Use `q` as the primary query parameter; `search_query` is accepted as an alias.
`hl` and `gl` localize ranking and result context; they default to `en` and `US`.
Named filters cover the public web search filters. Account-only chips such as Watched and Unwatched are not exposed.

parameters.name: q

parameters.name: search_query

parameters.description: Pagination token returned by a previous request
parameters.name: continuation_token

parameters.name: type

parameters.description: Sort results
parameters.name: sort_by

parameters.description: Filter by upload date
parameters.name: upload_date

get.description:
Returns transcript segments for a YouTube video using YouTube's native player captions.
Set `format=text`, `format=srt`, or `format=vtt` to receive plain-text output instead of the standard response envelope.
Returns `404` when the video currently has no transcript/captions available in any language — this is a normal, non-retryable result, not an error condition.
Returns `503` when the request is temporarily blocked or rate-limited; retrying after a short delay may succeed.
